docs.title: React Admin Dashboard
docs.text:
Developer documentation for a front-end admin dashboard built with React 19 and TypeScript. This guide describes the project as it exists in the source code today.

On this page

  • What it is
  • Project status
  • What works today
  • Technology
  • Requirements
  • Where to go next

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
The React Admin Dashboard is a single-page application for viewing and editing business data such as products and customers. It is organised by feature and separates data that comes from a server (server state) from data that only the interface needs (client state).

The project is also a working study of scalable front-end patterns: feature-based folders, reusable data-fetching wrappers, store slices, optimistic updates with an undo window, and live updates over server-sent events.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
Proof of concept

Only the product table and its editing workflow are developed in depth. Other areas, such as the Customers page, are partly built. Areas that are incomplete are listed on the Known limitations page of this guide.

docs.title: What works today
docs.text:
Area Where What it does Home dashboard /home Four panels: Weekly Summary cards, Weekly Sales Highlights, Product Inventory table and a Weekly Sales Overview chart Product table Home, Product Inventory panel Data grid with row selection, loading skeletons, a refreshing indicator and an error message Edit one product Product table, edit button Dialog form; saving shows a confirmation message and starts a 10-second undo window before the change is sent to the server Edit several products Product table, Edit Selected (enabled when two or more rows are selected) Accordion form with Save All Changes, which sends one bulk update request Live updates Product table Product additions and updates pushed by the server appear in the table without a reload Customers page /customers Same panel layout with a customers table Theme Header Light and dark mode toggle Offline banner Top of the page Shown when the browser reports that it is offline Notifications Side drawer and bottom of the page Notification drawer and a snackbar with an Undo action

Sample data in the chart

The Weekly Sales Overview chart uses four weeks of fixed sample data written into the component. It does not read from the server.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: The dashboard does not include a server. It requests its data from a REST API at http://localhost:3000, so a compatible API must be running for the tables to load. The endpoints the front end expects are described in the API reference.

docs.title: About this view
docs.text:
• The description is the same contract as the API reference, in a standard machine-readable format. You can download openapi.yaml and open it in any OpenAPI tool.
  • It describes what the front end sends and reads. It was not generated from a running server.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The dashboard has no server of its own. This page lists the HTTP endpoints that the front end calls, with the request and response shapes the code expects. Use it to build or check a compatible backend. The same contract is available as an OpenAPI file and in the API explorer.

How this page was written

This is the contract the front end expects, taken from the dashboard's source code. It is not generated from a running server. Field names marked (confirm) are read by the code but their exact form depends on the backend.

On this page

  • Conventions
  • Endpoint summary
  • Products
  • Product by id
  • Update a product
  • Bulk update products
  • Live product events
  • Customers
  • Data shapes
  • Notes for backend developers

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Base address: http://localhost:3000
  • Format: JSON for request and response bodies. Requests with a body send Content-Type: application/json.
  • Authentication: none. The front end sends no credentials or tokens.
  • Errors: any non-successful status (outside 200 to 299) is treated as a failure. The dashboard shows "Request failed: status" for list requests and "Update failed" or "Bulk update failed" for edits. Error bodies are not read.

docs.title: Endpoint summary
docs.text: Method Path Used for GET /api/products Products list for the summary cards and alerts GET //products Products list for the product table (see notes) GET /api/products/add/:id One product, loaded when an edit dialog opens PATCH /api/products/add/:id Update one product PATCH /api/products/bulk Update several products GET /api/products/stream Live product events (server-sent events) GET /api/users Customers list

docs.title: GET /api/products
docs.text:
Returns an array of products.

Response 200

[
  {
    "_id": "6970c12c0576869a149e11fe",
    "name": "Wireless Headphones",
    "category": "Electronics",
    "price": 512,
    "stock": 25,
    "status": "active",
    "unitsSold": 13,
    "revenue": 781,
    "unitsSoldChangePct": 0,
    "revenueChangePct": 0,
    "userType": "All",
    "region": "All"
  }
]

The example values are illustrative. The front end copies _id into id for every product it loads. See Product for each field.

docs.title: GET //products
docs.text: The product table requests this address, built from http://localhost:3000/ plus /products (note the double slash). It expects the same array as GET /api/products and stores it under the same cache key, so both requests fill the same table data. See the notes.

docs.title: GET /api/products/add/:id
docs.text:
Returns one product. Called when the edit dialog opens for a row.

Parameter In Description id Path The product's identifier

Response 200: a single Product object.

docs.title: PATCH /api/products/add/:id
docs.text:
Updates one product. Called after the 10-second undo window ends.

Request body: the product fields from the edit form, with id.

{
  "id": "6970c12c0576869a149e11fe",
  "name": "Wireless Headphones",
  "category": ["Electronics"],
  "price": 512,
  "stock": 25,
  "description": "Over-ear, Bluetooth"
}

Category format

The edit form always sends category as an array of strings, even for one category.

Response 200: the updated product. The front end reads _id or id, name, category, stock, price and status. If status is not "active" or "inactive", the product is treated as "inactive".

docs.title: PATCH /api/products/bulk
docs.text:
Updates several products in one request. Called by Save All Changes in the multiple-product edit form. Only rows the user changed are included, and each item carries only editable fields (createdAt, updatedAt and _id are removed before sending).

Request body

{
  "updates": [
    { "id": "6970c12c0576869a149e11fe", "name": "Wireless Headphones", "price": 499 },
    { "id": "697444e278bc2ef120f5a02a", "stock": 40 }
  ]
}

Response 200

{
  "success": [],
  "failed": []
}

The front end reads only failed. If it is a non-empty array, the dashboard writes the failed items to the browser console. The shape of each entry in success and failed is not read. (confirm)

docs.title: GET /api/products/stream
docs.text:
Opens a server-sent events (SSE) stream. The front end listens for two named events and expects each event's data to be a JSON product.

Event Front-end behaviour productAdded Adds the product to the products list if no product with the same id exists productUpdated Replaces the product whose id matches

Example productAdded event

event: productAdded
data: {"_id":"697444e278bc2ef120f5a02a","name":"CineBar 24W Portable Wireless Soundbar","category":"Electronics","price":512,"stock":0,"status":"active","createdAt":"2026-01-24T04:04:50.341Z","updatedAt":"2026-01-24T04:04:50.341Z","__v":0}

For productAdded, the front end reads _id or id, name, category, stock, userType and region, and fills unitsSold, revenue and the change percentages with fixed placeholder values.

For productUpdated, the front end compares the event's id with each product's id, so send id (not _id) in this event.

If the connection errors, the front end closes it and does not reconnect.

docs.title: GET /api/users
docs.text:
Returns an array of customers.

Response 200

[
  {
    "_id": "65f1c0ab12cd34ef56789012",
    "name": "Asha Rao",
    "email": "asha@example.com",
    "phone": 9876543210,
    "address": { "street": "12 MG Road", "city": "Bengaluru", "pin": "560001" },
    "region": "Asia-Pacific",
    "preferredPaymentMethod": "UPI",
    "totalOrders": 12,
    "totalRevenue": 8450,
    "status": "active"
  }
]

The example values are illustrative. The customers table joins the values of address into one comma-separated string, so address must be an object (a missing address causes an error).

docs.title: Product
docs.text: Field Type Used by Notes _id or id string All product views _id is copied into id on load name string Table, edit forms, summary category string or string[] Table, edit forms, summary tooltip The edit form sends an array price number Edit forms stock number Edit forms, low-stock summary The table column is named stockLevel (confirm) status "active", "inactive" or "pending" Edit forms Other values become "inactive" description string, optional Edit forms unitsSold number Table, alerts revenue number Table, alerts, summary unitsSoldChangePct number Summary revenueChangePct number Summary userType string Summary tooltip region string Table, summary createdAt, updatedAt ISO 8601 string Not displayed Removed from bulk updates

docs.title: Customer
docs.text: Field Type Notes _id string Copied to id in the table name, email, region string phone number address object Values are joined into one string preferredPaymentMethod "Card", "UPI", "PayPal" or "Credit Card" totalOrders, totalRevenue number status string One of active, inactive, pending, suspended, banned, deleted

docs.title: Notes for backend developers
docs.text:
• Two product list addresses. The summary and alerts request /api/products; the product table requests //products. Both write to the same cache entry, so make both addresses return the same list, or expect whichever answers last to fill the table.
  • Cache lifetime. The front end caches lists for 5 minutes and saves them in the browser for up to 24 hours, so changes made directly in the database may not appear immediately.
  • CORS. Allow the dashboard's origin, because the dashboard and API use different ports.
  • Field names. The front end tolerates _id and id for products, but the products table column is called stockLevel while the edit forms use stock. Confirm which name your API returns.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This page explains how the application is assembled, how pages are composed, and how the source code is organised.

On this page

  • Application shell
  • Routing
  • Page composition
  • Folder structure
  • Anatomy of a feature
  • Data flow at a glance
  • Styling

docs.title: Application shell
docs.text:
The app starts in src/main.tsx, which renders App inside React StrictMode and the theme provider. App (src/App.tsx) then adds data caching, routing and the always-visible interface.

StrictMode
└── AppThemeProvider            MUI light/dark theme and CssBaseline
    └── App
        ├── PersistQueryClientProvider   React Query client with localStorage persistence
        │   └── BrowserRouter
        │       ├── OfflineBanner        offline message
        │       ├── Header (NavBar)      logo, navigation, user menu, theme toggle
        │       ├── NotificationDrawer   side drawer
        │       ├── SnackbarComponent    messages with an Undo action
        │       └── Routes               the current page
        └── ReactQueryDevtools           open by default

Developer tools

React Query Devtools are rendered with initialIsOpen={true}, so the panel opens automatically in development. Change this value in App.tsx if you prefer it closed.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
Routing uses React Router (BrowserRouter). Two routes are defined.

Path Component Page /home MainBody Products dashboard /customers UsersMainBody Customers dashboard

The navigation bar lists Home, Products, Orders, Customers, Reports and Settings, and builds each link from the label (for example /orders). Only /home and /customers have matching routes, so the other links, and the root path /, currently render no page content.

docs.title: Page composition
docs.text:
Each page is a grid of independent panels. Every panel is loaded lazily with React.lazy and wrapped in ErrorSuspenceWrapper (components/common/wrapper.tsx), which combines two protections:

  • A Suspense boundary shows a Loading placeholder while the panel's code downloads.
  • An error boundary catches rendering errors and shows "panel name failed to load", so one failing panel does not break the page.

docs.title: Home page panels
docs.text:
Panel Component Layout Summary feature/summary/Summary One column on small screens, half width from the md breakpoint Alerts AlertsPanel Same as Summary Product Table feature/products/ProductTable Full width from the md breakpoint Products Chart ProductsChart Full width from the md breakpoint

The home page is configured by a panels array in components/main/body.tsx. To add a panel, add an entry with a name, a lazy component and optional column-span and minimum-height settings.

The Customers page (components/users/body.tsx) uses the same pattern with Summary, Alerts, a customers table and the shared Products Chart.

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
src/
├── main.tsx, App.tsx          entry point and application shell
├── components/
│   ├── common/                shared building blocks (wrappers, dialogs, skeletons, notifications)
│   ├── feature/
│   │   ├── products/          the products feature (see below)
│   │   └── summary/           summary cards for the home page
│   ├── layout/                header, navigation, notification drawer
│   ├── main/                  home page composition
│   └── users/                 customers page and its panels
├── store/                     Zustand store and slices shared across the app
├── theme/                     MUI light and dark themes, theme context, toggle
├── context/                   React context (product categories)
├── types/                     shared TypeScript types
└── mock/                      sample data from early development (not imported by the app)

The components/common folder holds code that more than one feature uses. Code that belongs to one feature stays inside that feature's folder.

docs.title: Anatomy of a feature
docs.text:
The products feature (components/feature/products/) shows the intended pattern:

products/
├── ProductTable.tsx           the feature's entry component
├── components/
│   ├── DataGrid.tsx           grid rendering, loading and error states
│   └── EditTable/             single and multiple product edit forms
├── hooks/                     data fetching, mutations, dialog logic, grid columns
├── store/                     the feature's Zustand store
├── types/                     feature-specific types
└── utils/                     helper functions

Tests sit next to the code they cover (for example productStore.test.tsx beside productStore.tsx).

docs.title: Data flow at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    API[(REST API<br/>localhost:3000)] -->|GET| RQ[React Query cache]
    API -. server-sent events .-> RQ
    RQ --> UI[Panels and tables]
    UI -->|edit| ST[Zustand stores]
    ST -->|optimistic update| RQ
    ST -->|PATCH after 10 s| API

Server data lives in the React Query cache and the interface reads from it. Edits first update the cache optimistically and are sent to the server after the undo window. See State management for the details.

docs.title: Styling
docs.text: Components and theming come from MUI. The theme (src/theme/index.ts) defines light and dark modes and adds a custom brand palette (main, soft, success, info, warning, error) used for accents. Tailwind CSS utility classes, enabled through the @tailwindcss/vite plugin, handle page layout such as the panel grid.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This page explains how to install, run, build and test the dashboard on your own computer.

On this page

  • Before you begin
  • Install
  • Start the API
  • Run the dashboard
  • Configuration
  • Scripts
  • Run the tests
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
You need:

  • Node.js version 20.19 or later (or 22.12 or later). This is the range Vite 7 requires.
  • npm, which is installed with Node.js.
  • A compatible REST API running at http://localhost:3000. The dashboard has no built-in server. The endpoints it expects are listed in the API reference.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and open the project folder.

    git clone https://github.com/rnijampure/react-admin-dashboard.git
cd react-admin-dashboard

  2. Install the dependencies.

    npm install

Missing immer package

The main store imports Zustand's Immer middleware (zustand/middleware/immer), which needs the immer package. immer is not listed in package.json. If the build reports that it cannot resolve immer, install it:

npm install immer

docs.title: Start the API
docs.text:
Start your backend so that it listens on port 3000. Two things must be true:

  • It serves the endpoints in the API reference.
  • It allows cross-origin requests from the dashboard's address (CORS), because the dashboard and the API run on different ports.

Without the API, the tables show an error message.

docs.title: Run the dashboard
docs.text:
npm run dev

Vite prints the local address, which is http://localhost:5173 unless that port is taken. Open it and go to /home. The root address / has no page, so enter /home or /customers in the address bar.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The project has no environment variables. Every API address is written into the source files, so to point the dashboard at a different server, edit these files.

File Address used components/feature/summary/Summary.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/products components/AlertsPanel.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/products components/feature/products/hooks/useProductsData.tsx http://localhost:3000/ plus an endpoint components/feature/products/hooks/useProductAction.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/products/add/:id and /api/products/bulk components/feature/products/hooks/useDialogActions.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/products/add/:id components/common/useProductsSSE.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/products/stream components/users/usersTable.tsx, users/summary/Summary.tsx, users/AlertsPanel.tsx http://localhost:3000/api/users

All paths are relative to src/.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
Command What it does npm run dev Starts the Vite development server with hot reload npm run build Type-checks with tsc -b, then creates a production build in dist/ npm run preview Serves the production build locally npm run lint Runs ESLint on the project npm test Runs the Vitest tests in watch mode npm run test:ui Opens the Vitest browser interface npm run test:coverage Runs the tests once and reports coverage

Extra test packages

test:ui and test:coverage need the @vitest/ui and @vitest/coverage-v8 packages, which are not in package.json. Vitest offers to install them the first time you run these commands.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
npm test

The project has three test files, each next to the code it covers:

File Covers products/store/productStore.test.tsx The product store: initial state, highlighting, dialog state, selection reset products/hooks/useProductsData.test.tsx The products data hook with a mocked query products/utils/utils.test.ts The product mapping helper

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause and fix Tables show "Something went wrong" or "Request failed" The API is not running on port 3000, or it returned an error. Start it and refresh. Browser console shows a CORS error Allow the dashboard's origin (for example http://localhost:5173) in the API. A red banner appears at the top The browser reports that it is offline. Check your network connection. Old data appears after you change the API The cache is saved in localStorage under RQ_CACHE for up to 24 hours. Clear that key, or change buster in App.tsx. Live updates stop The live-update connection closes after an error and does not reconnect. Reload the page. Navigation links such as Orders show a blank page Only /home and /customers have routes.

docs.title: State management
docs.text:
The dashboard keeps server state (data that lives on the server) and client state (data only the interface needs) in separate tools. This page describes both, and the undo workflow that connects them.

On this page

  • Two kinds of state
  • Server state with React Query
  • Live updates
  • Client state with Zustand
  • The undo workflow
  • Behaviour to be aware of

docs.title: Two kinds of state
docs.text:
Server state Client state Examples Products, customers Selected rows, open dialog, highlighted row, notification message Owner React Query cache Zustand stores Source of truth The server The browser Cached or persisted Yes (see below) No

Keeping the two apart means the interface never copies server data into a second store, so there is one place to look for each kind of value.

docs.title: Global defaults
docs.text:
App.tsx creates the query client with these defaults.

Option Value Meaning staleTime 5 minutes Data is treated as fresh for 5 minutes gcTime 24 hours Unused cached data is kept for 24 hours refetchOnWindowFocus true Data refreshes when the browser tab regains focus

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text: The cache is saved to the browser's localStorage under the key RQ_CACHE through PersistQueryClientProvider. Saved data expires after 24 hours (maxAge). The buster value is "v1": change it to discard every user's saved cache after a data-shape change.

docs.title: The useTanQueryGET wrapper
docs.text:
Components fetch data through useTanQueryGET (components/common/queryWrapper.tsx) rather than calling useQuery directly.

useTanQueryGET<T>(queryKey, queryFnURL, select?)
Parameter Description queryKey One of "products", "orders", "users" inside an array, for example ["products"] queryFnURL The URL to request with fetch select Optional function that transforms the data after normalisation

The wrapper:

  1. Throws an error such as Request failed: 500 when the response is not successful.
  2. Normalises data for the products key by copying MongoDB-style _id values into id.
  3. Applies the optional select function.
  4. Uses a 5-minute staleTime, refetches on window focus and does not retry failed requests (retry: false).

docs.title: Query keys
docs.text: Key Holds ["products"] The list of products ["product", id] One product, loaded when its edit dialog opens ["users"] The list of customers

docs.title: Live updates
docs.text:
useProductsSSE (components/common/useProductsSSE.tsx) opens a server-sent events connection to /api/products/stream and writes incoming data into the ["products"] cache.

Event Effect on the cache productAdded Adds the product to the list unless a product with the same id exists productUpdated Replaces the product with the matching id

The connection closes when the component unmounts. If the connection reports an error, the hook closes it and does not reconnect, so reload the page to resume live updates.

docs.title: Client state with Zustand
docs.text: There are three Zustand stores.

docs.title: Bound store
docs.text:
useBoundStore (store/useBoundStore.tsx) combines three slices into one store with the Immer middleware.

Slice State Actions Drawer isDrawerOpen (starts true) openDrawer, closeDrawer, toggleDrawer Notification notification with isOpen, message, severity notify(message, severity?), closeNotification Edit pendingMutation with NewProduct, OldProduct, timerId stageEdit, cancelEdit

severity is "success", "error", "info" or "warning"; notify accepts the first three and defaults to "info".

docs.title: Product store
docs.text:
useProductStore (components/feature/products/store/productStore.tsx) holds interface state for the product table.

State Purpose selectionModel Rows selected in the grid highlightedId Row currently flashing after an update editingProducts Products in the open edit dialog isDialogOpen Whether the edit dialog is open

Its actions are grouped under an actions object: setSelectionModel, setHighlightedId, setEditingProducts, setDialogOpen, flashRow(id, duration = 2500) and resetSelection. flashRow sets highlightedId and clears it after the duration, in milliseconds.

Reading actions

Some components currently read these actions from the store root (for example state.flashRow) instead of from state.actions. See the Known limitations page.

docs.title: Countdown store
docs.text: useCountdownStore (components/common/notifications/countdownStore.ts) provides a one-second countdown: startCountdown(duration, onComplete) and stopCountdown(), with timeLeft and timerId state. No rendered component uses it at present.

docs.title: The undo workflow
docs.text:
Saving a single product does not send the change to the server immediately. It is staged for 10 seconds so the user can undo it.

  1. The user saves the edit form. A success message appears in the snackbar.
  2. stageEdit clears any earlier pending timer, cancels in-flight ["products"] queries so they cannot overwrite the cache, and stores the previous version of the product.
  3. The cache is updated at once with the edited product (an optimistic update), so the table shows the change immediately.
  4. A 10-second timer starts.
  5. If the timer ends, the saved change is sent to the server with a PATCH request, and the pending edit is cleared. On success the products list is refetched and the row is marked for highlighting.
  6. If the user chooses Undo, cancelEdit restores the previous product in the cache, stops the timer and clears the pending edit. Nothing is sent to the server.

If the server rejects the request, the mutation's onError handler restores the products list as it was before the edit.

Editing several products with Save All Changes works differently: it sends one bulk PATCH request straight away, with no undo window, and refetches the products list when it finishes.

docs.title: Behaviour to be aware of
docs.text:
• Only one staged edit is held at a time. Staging a second edit before the first one's 10 seconds have passed clears the first edit's timer, so the first edit is not sent to the server, although its change stays visible in the cache until the next refetch.
  • The snackbar closes after 10 seconds, the same length as the undo window.
  • Reloading the page during the undo window cancels the pending save, because the timer exists only in memory, so the change is never sent to the server.
